LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen a long way — it's down more than a third from its high and sitting right near its lowest point of the year — but nothing has broken in the business; defense spending keeps flowing, and it's always been the cheapest of the big defense contractors.

ASML.sentence: ASML nudged up again, and the good news is its profits are finally starting to grow into its lofty price rather than running on pure hype, since it's still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet, uneventful stretch — the world's biggest industrial gas supplier keeps humming along on long-term contracts, and it's unusually priced right in line with peers for once, which rarely happens for the best operator in the group.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft had a strong day, and the story is unchanged — their Azure cloud business keeps growing fast on the back of AI demand, without much drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher slipped a touch, but biotech funding is thawing again, and since more lab funding eventually means more orders for their equipment, that's a good sign — though the stock is already near its yearly high.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge dipped slightly; it's paying a hefty dividend, though part of that is just because interest rates are unusually high right now, so the payout is generous but not screaming cheap.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow eased back a bit and is down nearly a third from its high, which is unusual for a company this strong — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI-assistant tools under long contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore was basically flat while copper prices have been surging, so this miner and trading house is lagging behind the metal it digs up — which could mean it has some catching up to do.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose after its update, and the key thing is the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still climbing about 4% — a headline figure that looked like prices fell was just a mix quirk, not a real drop.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is calm — its fortunes swing most with the Mexican peso, and the peso is sitting right in the middle of its range, so nothing's pushing this one either way.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras dipped a little, but oil prices are running far above what it costs them to pull it out of the ground, which comfortably funds that very large dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container shipping giant that moves goods across the oceans, gained a bit and is trading for less than its fleet of ships would cost to replace — a classic sign of a cheap, cyclical business.

MA.sentence: Mastercard barely moved and is oddly priced almost identically to Visa even though it's growing faster, so you're essentially getting the quicker-growing of the two payment networks at no extra cost.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker edged up and is down about a third from its high, but that drop is really about worry across the whole medical-device sector rather than anything specific to this company, which keeps outpacing its rivals.
